title: Artemis II Crew at Canadian Space Agency HQ — Public Virtual Livestream (Day 2 of Canada Tour)
detail: Day 2 of the Artemis II crew's Canadian tour brought all five mission participants to the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) headquarters in Saint-Hubert, Quebec on May 14, 2026. The CSA hosted a public virtual event from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM ET — broadcast live on the CSA's YouTube channel and Facebook page — during which Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen (joined by CSA Capcom Jenni Gibbons) shared reflections on the Artemis II mission and answered questions from audiences across Canada and internationally. The format was bilingual (English/French) and included outreach to youth and Indigenous communities. The Saint-Hubert event followed the Ottawa portion of the tour (May 13: PM Carney meeting, Canadian Museum of Nature, sold-out National Arts Centre event) and precedes the Montreal stop (May 15, ticketed talk at Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier, Place des Arts). The crew's Canadian visit is anchored by Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — who on April 6, 2026, at 1:56 p.m. EDT, became the farthest non-American from Earth in history (252,706 miles) as part of the first crewed lunar flyby in more than 50 years. CSA headquarters, at 6767 route de l'Aéroport in Saint-Hubert (Montreal suburb), is home to Canada's astronaut office and the development program for Canadarm3.

title: Artemis III SLS Core Stage Stacking Advances in VAB High Bay 2 — Day 34 Post-Splashdown
detail: Day 34 post-Artemis II splashdown (April 10, 2026): NASA's next-mission hardware stack is actively progressing at Kennedy Space Center. The Artemis III SLS core stage — the tank section mated to its four RS-25 engine section — is in VAB High Bay 2 at KSC (visible in recent photography) for integration ahead of the Artemis III mission targeting late 2027. In parallel, the Artemis III Orion service module (built by Airbus for ESA) completed acoustic testing at KSC's Operations and Checkout Facility (O&C) in early May 2026, a key verification milestone for the spacecraft's structural integrity under launch acoustic loads. Artemis III is officially redesignated as an Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test — Orion will rendezvous with the SpaceX Starship Human Landing System (HLS) in a 460 km orbit to verify crew interfaces and docking procedures — with Artemis IV (targeting 2028) slated as the first crewed lunar surface landing. Simultaneously, at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility, the Artemis II Orion crew module continues heat shield visual inspection; formal X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center are on track for summer 2026.
